indicators.description: new-.--------------------AFRICARICE --- (MEDIUM MATURITY RAINFED LOWLAND) ----(varietal development).-------- KEY ACTIVITIES FOR THIS DELIVERABLE: AfricaRice-B4T_05 ----- The objective is to develop, validate, and disseminate a new generation of market-driven, climate-resilient, and high-yielding rainfed lowland rice varieties targeting the TMeLS-R and TMeLF-R market segments across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with the potential to sustainably increase productivity over 5.1 million hectares ofrainfed lowland land. The program leverages modern breeding tools and data-driven approaches to accelerate variety development. Using the Rapid Generation Advance (RGA) system combined with the Single Seed Descent (SSD) method, a three-year breeding cycle from crossing to yield testing is achieved cutting development time by over 50%. A structured six-year product development cycle integrates mid-density genotyping, QTL profiling for key adaptive traits (Drought tolerance, flooding tolerance, and grain quality), disease screening, and multilocation yield testing. On-farm trials are conducted with NARES partners across SSA under the Breeding Task Force framework to ensure wide adaptability, end-user preference, and market alignment.-------- BREEDING PIPELINE: BP00114(TMeLF-R) .-------- MARKET SEGMENT: WAF MS00339,CAF MS00145,EAF MS00283 ---------------------INDICATOR: Number of varieties released to partners for scaling
countries: The Democratic Republic of the Congo

indicators.label: CIAT (Alliance) — HLO7.AOW2.IO2 (custom)
indicators.description: 24-.----------------CIAT - CASSAVA ---------------Cassava Sweet CIAT BP00217 and Cassava CIAT BP00218—using a within-family recurrent genomic selection strategy that leverages genomic resources for product extraction and applies controlled inbreeding to generate inbred or partially inbred founders to replace the highly heterozygous base population. All outputs center on reducing breeding cycle time, with progress measured against the 2025 baseline. The primary deliverable is a 25% reduction in breeding cycle time. ------------------.-------- KEY ACTIVITIES FOR THIS DELIVERABLE: Design and implement optimized cassava breeding schemes for fresh (BP00217) and processing (BP00218) pipelines using within-family recurrent genomic selection (wfRGS) to accelerate genetic gain and product extraction. Activities include restructuring pipelines to shorten generation intervals, integrating genomic prediction into parent selection and advancement decisions, and applying controlled inbreeding (e.g., S₁/S₂) to develop partially inbred founders that replace highly heterozygous base populations. Crossing designs and family structures are refined to maximize recombination, with early-stage genomic selection enabling faster advancement. Implementation is coordinated across regions (WAF, EAF, LAC, SEA), with initial deployment in Vietnam and Colombia, supported by harmonized data systems, genotyping workflows, and decision-support tools. Progress is benchmarked against the 2025 baseline, targeting a ≥25% reduction in breeding cycle time..-------- BREEDING PIPELINE: Cassava Sweet CIAT BP00217: Fresh market cassava (wfRGS; global); Cassava CIAT BP00218: Processing cassava (wfRGS; global).-------- MARKET SEGMENT: Cassava WAF MS00880; Cassava WAF MS00884; Cassava EAF MS00890; Cassava EAF MS00892; Cassava EAF MS00893; Cassava WAF MS01065; Cassava LAC MS00900; Cassava LAC MS00901; Cassava SEA MS00909 .-------- INDICATOR: Number of breeding pipelines in which the cycle time was reduced from …

indicators.description: 9b---- CIP - CROP AGNOSTIC - (Evidence-based targeting of producer and consumer segments..-------- KEY ACTIVITIES FOR THIS DELIVERABLE: TRENT/VIVIAN Title: Modeling and policy analysis on Purple Top Disease Complex. Description: This package will conduct integrated modeling and policy analysis to assess the potential agronomic, economic, and social impacts of the emerging Purple Top disease complex, which is increasingly affecting potato and other Solanaceous crops such as tomatoes, peppers, and golden berries. By combining disease spread modeling with forward-looking assessments of production and market dynamics, this work will estimate the potential consequences of inaction—if resistant varieties are not adopted and phytosanitary measures are not implemented—on productivity, food security, and smallholder livelihoods. Key activities will include: (1) developing a spatial model of disease spread; (2) preparing preliminary reports on the projected impacts on yields, markets, and rural incomes; (3) conducting a policy analysis to identify and evaluate measures that deter the disease’s spread; and (4) producing policy briefs and recommendations to guide seed distribution, strengthen phytosanitary practices, and limit negative outcomes. By 2026, outputs will include a validated disease impact model, forward-looking impact analyses, and policy briefs to inform pipeline investment case calculations. This package supports 2030 Outcomes 1 and 3 (adoption of resilient varieties and improved systems for risk mitigation) and contributes to HLO1 “Steer to Impact” and HLO6 “Refocus to Markets.” It is highly relevant to impact indicators on climate adaptation, food security, and poverty reduction, providing evidence to guide proactive responses to emerging biotic threats. .-------- BREEDING PIPELINE: CIP BP00249; CIP BP0049.-------- MARKET SEGMENT: MS00807; MS00716; MS00806.-------- INDICATOR: Number of knowledge products (disaggregated by type, policy brief)

indicators.description: 39.---- CIP POTATO - Characterization of advanced potato germplasm for iron content completed.....-------- KEY ACTIVITIES FOR THIS DELIVERABLE: MOCTAR/MARIELA/GABRIELA Title: Mainstreaming iron (Fe) content in potato breeding for South Asian market segments Description: This activity implements a targeted evaluation and selection pipeline to integrate iron (Fe) content into agronomically competitive potato germplasm aligned with the target product profiles (TPPs) of the South Asian market. Advanced clones and breeding parents were preselected based on historical multi-environment performance for Fe concentration, marketable yield, and key agronomic and quality traits. A full-factorial crossing scheme (all × all) is being conducted to maximize recombination and generate a comprehensive set of families. In parallel, the approximately 55 potential parents will be evaluated across five representative environments, generating phenotypic data on yield and TPP-relevant traits. Tuber samples will be collected and analyzed under controlled laboratory conditions to quantify Fe content. These datasets will form the basis for integrated selection. Genomic prediction for cross performance (GPCP) will be applied across all parental combinations, using Fe content and marketable yield as primary traits within a multi-trait framework. Advancement decisions will be based on the combined assessment of observed field performance, laboratory-derived Fe values, predicted cross means and variances, and alignment with TPP requirements, with explicit management of yield–nutrition trade-offs. The key activities included (1) parental preselection and cross combinations; (2) multi-location field evaluation of potential founders; (3) laboratory quantification of Fe content; (4) GPCP analysis of all parental combinations; and (5) selection of priority families for advancement. By the end of the year, selected families are defined, TPS availability is consolidated where required, and prioritized…

indicators.description: 91.----CIP - Potato, sweetpotato, cassava - (Operationalization of the Kenya Seeds and Plant Varieties (Vegetatively Propagating Crops) Regulations. Focus on materials that respond to market segments prioritized by breeders.)..-------- KEY ACTIVITIES FOR THIS DELIVERABLE: KWAME/JORGE: Two stakeholder meetings to discuss the next steps for the Kenya Act for Vegetatively Propagating Seeds. The first meeting will be an internal meeting involving CGIAR staff from CIP, IFPRI and IITA. The second meeting will be broader involving several national stakeholders e.g., KEPHIS, KALRO, CABE, MoA, AG's office etc. Currently, the Act is on hold following a high court ruling that suspended the Kenya Plant and Varieties Act. The VPS Act is likely to suffer the same consequences because of similar clauses to those that were contested in court e.g., registration of seed merchants. The Attorney General's office advised that the Act be put on hold until an appeal involving the Plant and Varieties Act is determined. The proposed meeting will enable stakeholders to reflect on the proceedings and forecast likely scenarios on the way forward. Two reports will be generated as deliverables..-------- BREEDING PIPELINE: This regulation is generic, but focus will be on current breeding pipelines for Africa: Sweetpotato: BP00054, BP00122, BP00053, BP00124; Potato: BP00049.-------- MARKET SEGMENT: This regulation is generic, but focus will be on current market segments for Africa: Sweetpotato: MS00725/728, MS00724, MS00719/720, MS00718/721; Potato: MS00716, MS00806.-------- INDICATOR: Number of knowledge products developed (disaggregated by type, report and policy brief)

Foresight is generated for key indicators (poverty, hunger and NCDs, diets, yield, area, demographics) towards 2050 for all CGIAR crops globally, at national and national-crop level.
